# std.websocket

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

WebSockets: client connections (`connect`), and the server side of an
upgraded request (`http.RequestScope.websocket`, `http.websocket_handler`).
Receiving and sending wait independently, so one task can read while
another writes. Pings are answered for you; `recv` gives `none` once the
peer closed.

### `Options`

```badger
pub type Options = { headers: Map<String, String>, max_message_bytes: Int }
```

Connection options: request headers (authorization, a subprotocol) and

### `WebSocket`

```badger
struct WebSocket { handle: native.Handle }
```

An open connection (closed once unreachable, or by `close`).

#### `WebSocket.close`

```badger
fn close(self: &Self) -> Result<Unit, Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

Close normally (code 1000).

#### `WebSocket.close_with`

```badger
fn close_with(self: &Self, code: Int, reason: String) -> Result<Unit, Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

Close with a status code (1000-4999) and a reason.

#### `WebSocket.recv`

```badger
fn recv(self: &Self) -> Result<Option<Message>, Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

The next message (waits); `none` once the peer closed.

#### `WebSocket.send`

```badger
fn send(self: &Self, message: Message) -> Result<Unit, Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

Send a message (waits while the peer is behind).

#### `WebSocket.send_binary`

```badger

```

#### `WebSocket.send_text`
